title: The eight, in depth
hookLine: the poor, the needy, collectors, hearts to be reconciled, freeing captives, debtors, Allah's cause, travelers (9:60)

lines: ONE VERSE, LIKE A GUEST LIST.
cards: A single verse, surah nine, verse sixty, and it reads like a guest list. Not a vague one. Not give to good causes.
It names who, one after another, and then it stops. Some of the names are obvious. Some are surprising.
One is a person who's simply far from home. You met this list on day one fifty-two, in one breath. Today, read slowly, two by two: the eight.

teach.b: Here's the verse in Pickthall's words: "The alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those who collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and to free the captives and the debtors, and for the cause of Allah, and (for) the wayfarer; a duty imposed by Allah."

First pair: the poor and the needy, al-fuqara' and al-masakin. Both lack enough, and scholars discuss which of the two is worse off, without one settled answer. Either way, they come first in the verse.
Second pair: those who collect it, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled. The collectors are paid from zakat for their work, so the system can run.
The hearts to be reconciled are people whose goodwill toward the community was being won, and scholars differ on how this door applies today.
Third pair: freeing captives, and debtors. Money that buys someone's freedom, and money that lifts a crushing debt off someone's back. Both get a person out from under something.
Fourth pair: the cause of Allah, and the wayfarer. Some scholars read the cause of Allah narrowly, others more broadly, and that difference matters for where zakat goes.
The wayfarer, ibn as-sabil, literally son of the road, is a traveler cut off from their money, even someone wealthy at home.

teach.h: THE ALMS ARE ONLY FOR THE POOR AND THE NEEDY.
teach.b: So zakat isn't only for people who are always poor. It's for anyone stranded. And notice the word only at the start.
The list is a boundary: these eight, and not just any good cause.

how: Muslims give zakat only to the eight kinds of recipients named in Qur'an 9:60, directly or through mosques and zakat organizations that distribute it among them.

games.q: you're on a long journey and your money is stolen. at home you're comfortable, but here you can't pay for a meal. does the verse include you?
o: no, because you're wealthy at home.
only if you're also in debt.
games.why: yes. the wayfarer, ibn as-sabil, is one of the eight: zakat is for anyone stranded, not only the always-poor.

practice: Go slowly through the doors, one per breath: the poor, the needy, someone in debt, someone far from home, and let a face or a place come with each, someone you know or have passed.
Notice which face stays with you longest; that's the door you might give through.

wordCard.voice: The eight. The people zakat is for, named in surah nine, verse sixty, from the poor to the wayfarer. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: eight doors. A person can walk through any one of them. Tomorrow: the fifth, a share some Muslims give alongside zakat.
